newsitem.title: ISRAEL: FORECAST: Israel Sept CPI seen up 0.5-0.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST: Israel Sept CPI seen up 0.5-0.6 pct.

text.p: Israel's consumer price index (CPI), due to be published on Tuesday, will post a rise of 0.5 to 0.6 percent following an increase of 0.4 percent in August, economists estimated.
In September 1995 the CPI rose 1.0 percent.
A rise of 0.5 percent, considered low for the month of September, would bring year-on-year inflation to 11.5 percent.

The Federation of Israeli Chambers of Commerce estimated the CPI rise at 0.6 percent. The federation's economists said clothing and footware prices fell by over one percent because of end-of-season sales while fruit and vegetable prices rose four to five percent.
Jonathan Katz, chief economist at Capital Holdings consultants, said housing prices are falling slightly and the relatively strong shekel has brought down the price of imports.
Katz predicted September inflation of 0.5 percent, the same as economists at Bank Hapoalim.
Katz said he believes a rise of 0.5 percent will prompt the central bank to lower interest rates by a token amount of 0.3 percentage point.
"There are increasingly more economic indicators pointing to an economic slowdown. People are even talking about a recession," Katz said.
He noted that the number of job seekers has increased sharply in the last six months while tourism has fallen.

"Money supply (growth) is also coming down," Katz said. Initial estimates are that M1 rose 1.5 to 1.6 percent in September. Normally the figure is much higher in September, when consumption rises due to a series of Jewish holidays.
Katz said M1 growth of nine percent in the last 12 months is considered very low.
